newsitem.title: JAPAN: Crude prices steady to firm in Asia after API data.
newsitem.headline: Crude prices steady to firm in Asia after API data.

text.p: Crude oil prices were steady to firm by midday in Asia on Wednesday after bullish weekly U.S. data on gasoline and crude oil stocks was released overnight, traders said.
U.S. gasoline stocks fell 3.50 million barrels in the week ended July 11 to 200.60 million barrels, the API said.
Crude oil stocks held in primary storage fell 5.43 million barrels to 317.23 million barrels, it said.
Cash September Brent was notionally assessed at $18.40/18.45 per barrel.
September Brent on SIMEX was untraded at 0305 GMT, and indicated at $18.39/18.55. The contract settled at $18.37 on London's IPE on Tuesday.
Meanwhile, August NYMEX light crude on the ACCESS after-hours system stood at $19.75/19.78, compared with the New York close of $19.67, where it gained 68 cents.
The Brent/Dubai spread was notionally assessed at $1.05/1.15 for September, similar to late U.S. trading levels.
The October Brent/Dubai spread was assessed at $1.07/1.17.
September/October Dubai was notionally assessed at -12/-7 cents and October/November at -10/-5 cents.
